label: Potential inspirations
summary: The list of potential inspirations shown in the inspirations window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source (datamodel) of a list in the inspirations window. The game does not document what 'potential' means exactly; this follows its name and that use.

label: Selected inspiration
summary: The inspiration the player has currently selected in the inspirations window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the window, and compares it (with an equality check) with each row's inspiration to decide what to show.

label: Sponsored inspirations
summary: The list of inspirations shown in the inspirations window that are already sponsored.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source (datamodel) of a list in the inspirations window. Going by its name and that use, these are the inspirations already being supported.

label: Has any inspirations
summary: Whether there is at least one potential or sponsored inspiration to show.
details: Vanilla uses it in the royal court window, together with other checks, to decide whether a part of that window is visible.

label: Has selected inspiration
summary: Whether an inspiration is currently selected in the inspirations window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide a part of the inspirations window.

label: Is new inspiration
summary: Whether the given inspiration counts as new in the inspirations window.
details: Vanilla passes the inspiration of the current list row and uses the result to show or hide something on that row. What makes an inspiration 'new' is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an inspiration, as vanilla writes Inspiration.Self

label: Clear new mark
summary: Removes the 'new' status of the given inspiration in the inspirations window.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it on click, with the inspiration of the current row. Going by its name and its pairing with the new-inspiration check.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an inspiration, as vanilla writes Inspiration.Self

label: Select inspiration
summary: Selects the given inspiration in the inspirations window.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla does not use it in any game text or GUI line; this follows its name only.

label: This window
summary: The inspirations window itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by the name: vanilla uses other types' .Self to hand the object itself to another function (for example Character.Self). No line uses this one.

label: Toggle inspiration
summary: Toggles the given inspiration in the inspirations window.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it on click with the inspiration of the current row. What exactly is toggled (for example selected or not) is not documented; this follows its name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an inspiration, as vanilla writes Inspiration.Self

label: This category item
summary: The interaction category entry itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more. Other types' AccessSelf is used in vanilla to hand a widget to a function.

label: Interaction category
summary: The character interaction category this entry stands for.
details: Vanilla reads its colour (GetColor) for a colour setting in the interaction templates.

label: Index
summary: The position number of this category entry, as a whole number.
details: No vanilla line uses it on this type, so the exact meaning (a position in the list) rests on its name.

label: Interactions
summary: The list of interactions inside this category.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source (datamodel) of a list in the interaction templates, going by its name a list of this category's interactions.

label: Category name
summary: The display name of this interaction category.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as a text in the interaction templates.

label: Has more highlighted
summary: Whether the category has more highlighted interactions than are shown.
details: Vanilla does not use it anywhere; this follows its name only, so the exact meaning is not certain.

label: Has more interactions
summary: Whether the category has more interactions than are currently shown.
details: Vanilla does not use it anywhere; this follows its name only, and it likely pairs with the 'show more' action.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether this category entry is shown in the interaction menu.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the category's row.

label: This category item
summary: The interaction category entry itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by the name: vanilla uses other types' .Self to hand the object itself to another function (for example Character.Self). No line uses this one.

label: Show more
summary: Expands the category to show more of its interactions.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla does not use it; this follows its name only.

label: This container
summary: The interaction container itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more.

label: Interactions
summary: The list of interactions held by this container.
details: No line uses it on this type. Vanilla uses a function of the same name on the category entry and on the puppet entry as a list source, so this is likely the same, going by its name.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether this container is shown.
details: No line uses it on this type. Other types' IsVisible are used in vanilla to show or hide GUI parts, so this is likely the same, going by its name.

label: This container
summary: The interaction container itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by the name: vanilla uses other types' .Self to hand the object itself to another function (for example Character.Self). No line uses this one.

label: This description
summary: The interaction effects description itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more.

label: Accept effects text
summary: The text describing what happens if the interaction is accepted.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it in the effects part of the interaction window.

label: Actor
summary: The character who starts the interaction.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context for a block of the effects description, so that block can show that character. The meaning of 'actor' as the initiator follows the game's usual wording.

label: Displayed effects
summary: The effects of the interaction that are displayed to the player.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of blocks in the interaction window, and in a visibility check on the confirmation window. What the returned object holds is not documented here.

label: Intermediary
summary: The character who acts as go-between in the interaction, if there is one.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the intermediary part of the effects description. Going by its name and that use.

label: Intermediary refusal text
summary: The text describing what happens if the intermediary refuses.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it in the effects part of the interaction window. Going by its name, it covers a refusal by the intermediary.

label: Recipient
summary: The character the interaction is aimed at.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context for a block of the effects description, so that block can show that character.

label: Refusal effects text
summary: The text describing what happens if the interaction is refused.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it in the effects part of the interaction window.

label: Has refusal effect
summary: Whether the interaction has effects that apply when it is refused.
details: Vanilla uses it, together with the check for a 'maybe' answer, to decide whether to show the refusal part of the effects. The migration window uses it alone to show or hide something.

label: Is intermediary shown
summary: Whether the intermediary part of the effects description is shown.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the intermediary block.

label: Is maybe answer
summary: Whether the answer to the interaction can still go either way.
details: Vanilla combines it with the refusal-effect check to decide whether to show the refusal part. The exact meaning of 'maybe' is not documented; this follows its name and that use.

label: Showing intermediary refusal
summary: Whether the intermediary's refusal effects are the ones currently shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button and to show or hide a part of the interaction window.

label: Showing accept effects
summary: Whether the effects of acceptance are the ones currently shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button and to show or hide a part of the grant-titles window.

label: Showing recipient refusal
summary: Whether the recipient's refusal effects are the ones currently shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button and to show or hide a part of the interaction window.

label: This description
summary: The interaction effects description itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by the name: vanilla uses other types' .Self to hand the object itself to another function (for example Character.Self). No line uses this one.

label: Show intermediary refusal
summary: Switches the effects view to the intermediary's refusal effects.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it on click, next to the matching showing-state check.

label: Show accept effects
summary: Switches the effects view to the effects of acceptance.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it on click, next to the matching showing-state check.

label: Show recipient refusal
summary: Switches the effects view to the recipient's refusal effects.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it on click, next to the matching showing-state check.

label: This interaction item
summary: The interaction entry itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more.

label: Checkbox enabled
summary: Whether the checkbox of this interaction entry can be clicked.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of the checkbox in the interaction list.

label: Accept tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about accepting this interaction.
details: Returns text. Vanilla does not use it; this follows its name only.

label: Character interaction
summary: The character interaction this entry stands for.
details: Vanilla asks it for its icon, passing the character the menu is open on.

label: Interaction category
summary: The category of the character interaction this entry stands for.
details: No line uses it on this type. Vanilla uses the same function on the category entry to get a colour, so this is likely the same kind of object, going by its name.

label: Checkbox frame
summary: The number of the picture frame the checkbox should show, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla compares it with 2 to decide whether the checkbox counts as checked.

label: Checkbox tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of this entry's checkbox.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of the checkbox.

label: Extra icon
summary: An extra icon picture for this interaction entry.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of an icon in the interaction list. See also the check for whether the extra icon is used.

label: Extra icon text
summary: The text that goes with the entry's extra icon.
details: Returns text. Vanilla does not use it; this follows its name only.

label: Interaction name
summary: The display name of this interaction entry.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as the row label and inside the favourites tooltip. The name GetName is used by many types in the game.

label: Preview scheme odds
summary: The predicted odds of the scheme this interaction would start, as a number.
details: Vanilla feeds it to a function that picks the picture frame for the odds level.

label: Scheme type
summary: The scheme type this interaction would start.
details: The game marks it as a promotion to the scheme type. Vanilla checks whether it is valid and uses it as the data context for showing scheme details.

label: Tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of this interaction entry.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as the row's tooltip.

label: Warning tooltip
summary: The tooltip text explaining the warning shown on this entry.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as a tooltip; the entry also has a check for a warning icon.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether this interaction entry has an icon.
details: No line uses it on this type. Other types' HasIcon are used in vanilla tooltips to show or hide an icon, so this is likely the same, going by its name.

label: Has preview odds
summary: Whether the interaction has scheme odds that can be previewed.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the odds display of an entry.

label: Has warning icon
summary: Whether this interaction entry shows a warning icon.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the warning icon.

label: Is character interaction
summary: Whether this entry is an ordinary character interaction.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to show different layouts for character interactions and for other kinds of entries in the list.

label: Is favourite
summary: Whether the player has marked this interaction as a favourite.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the favourite button and to choose between the 'add to favourites' and 'remove from favourites' tooltips.

label: Is highlighted
summary: Whether this interaction entry is highlighted.
details: Vanilla combines it with 'not a puppet interaction' to decide whether to show a highlight. What causes a highlight is not documented.

label: Is marriage setting
summary: Whether this entry is a marriage setting rather than a normal interaction.
details: Vanilla uses it and its negation to show different parts of the entry. Going by its name and that use.

label: Is 'more' entry
summary: Whether this entry is the 'more' row that expands the list.
details: Vanilla uses it together with the potential-accept check to hide parts of an ordinary entry. Going by its name and that use.

label: Is potential accept
summary: Whether this entry is a 'potential accept' entry.
details: Vanilla uses it together with the 'more' check to hide parts of an ordinary entry. The exact meaning is not documented.

label: Is puppet interaction
summary: Whether this entry is an interaction done through a puppet character.
details: Vanilla uses it to hide the highlight, and to show a part only when the puppet view is not active. Going by its name and those uses.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the player can currently use this interaction.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or enable the entry, and to colour its name as clickable or greyed out.

label: On click
summary: Runs the entry's click action.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it when the player clicks the entry. What exactly happens depends on the entry.

label: On checkbox click
summary: Runs the action of the entry's checkbox.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it when the checkbox is clicked.

label: This interaction item
summary: The interaction entry itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by the name: vanilla uses other types' .Self to hand the object itself to another function (for example Character.Self). No line uses this one.

label: Uses extra icon
summary: Whether the entry should show its extra icon.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the extra icon.

label: Toggle favourite
summary: Adds the interaction to the player's favourites, or removes it if it is already there.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it when the favourite button is clicked.

label: This effect entry
summary: The 'other effect' entry itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more.

label: Character
summary: The character this effect entry is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a row in the interaction effects list, so the row can show that character. Check HasCharacter first, as an entry may have none.

label: Effect text
summary: The text describing this effect.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it in the interaction effects list.

label: List tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for an effect entry that stands for a list of characters.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the effects list; see the check for whether the entry is a list.

label: Has character
summary: Whether this effect entry names a character.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the character part of the row.

label: Is list
summary: Whether this effect entry stands for several characters rather than one.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide a part of the row. Going by its name and the matching list tooltip.

label: This effect entry
summary: The 'other effect' entry itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by the name: vanilla uses other types' .Self to hand the object itself to another function (for example Character.Self). No line uses this one.

label: This effects object
summary: The participants' effects object itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more.

label: Actor effect text
summary: The text describing what the interaction does to the actor, the one who starts it.
details: Returns text. No line uses it by this exact type, but a line in the interaction window reads it from the displayed effects as a text. Going by its name.

label: Intermediary effect text
summary: The text describing what the interaction does to the intermediary.
details: Returns text. A line in the interaction window shows it as a text, reached through the displayed effects. Going by its name.

label: Other effects
summary: The list of further effect entries of the interaction, beyond the actor's, recipient's and intermediary's texts.
details: A line in the interaction window uses it as a list source, reached through the displayed effects. Going by its name; the game documents nothing more.

label: Recipient effect text
summary: The text describing what the interaction does to the recipient, the one it is aimed at.
details: Returns text. A line in the interaction window shows it as a text, reached through the displayed effects. Going by its name.

label: This effects object
summary: The participants' effects object itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by the name: vanilla uses other types' .Self to hand the object itself to another function (for example Character.Self). No line uses this one.

label: This scheme info
summary: The scheme prediction info itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more.

label: Potential agents text
summary: A text listing the agents predicted to join the scheme.
details: Returns text. Vanilla puts it under the heading of the predicted-agents tooltip of a scheme.

label: Artifact
summary: The artifact connected to the scheme, if there is one.
details: No line uses it on this type; the lines found use a similar name on other types. This follows its name only.

label: Discovery text
summary: The text describing what happens if the scheme is discovered.
details: Returns text. Vanilla does not use it directly; it does use a matching check for whether such a text exists. Going by its name.

label: Scheme name
summary: The display name of the scheme.
details: Returns text. No line uses it on this type; GetName is used by many types in the game, so this follows its name only.

label: Potential agent count
summary: How many agents are predicted to join the scheme, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the 'Predicted Agents' line of the scheme prediction.

label: Odds breakdown
summary: The detailed breakdown behind the predicted odds of the scheme.
details: A line in the confirmation window uses it as a data context to show the breakdown. Going by its name and that use.

label: Predicted odds
summary: The predicted odds of the scheme, as a number.
details: Vanilla turns it into a difficulty level name and a picture frame, and a debug text prints it raw.

label: Scheme owner
summary: The character who would run the scheme.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the scheme prediction, so that part can show the character. Going by its name and that use.

label: Replaced scheme
summary: The existing scheme that a new one would abandon.
details: Vanilla uses it in the warning text shown when starting a new scheme would replace a running one.

label: Scheme
summary: The scheme the interaction would start.
details: Vanilla uses it to read the scheme's action name and category name in texts, and as a data context in the GUI.

label: Phase length in days
summary: How many days one phase of the scheme lasts, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla passes it to a duration formatter in the 'scheme speed' line of the prediction.

label: Secrecy
summary: The predicted secrecy of the scheme, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a percentage in the scheme prediction.

label: Secrecy breakdown
summary: A text breaking down what makes up the predicted secrecy.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it under the secrecy line of the scheme prediction tooltip.

label: Secrecy with option
summary: The predicted secrecy of the scheme with a chosen option applied.
details: Vanilla does not use it; this follows its name only, so what 'option' means is not certain.

label: Success breakdown
summary: A text breaking down what makes up the predicted success chance.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it in the success chance tooltip of the scheme prediction.

label: Success chance
summary: The predicted initial chance that the scheme succeeds, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a percentage in the scheme prediction tooltip and compares it to decide which extra text to show.

label: Success chance with option
summary: The predicted success chance of the scheme with a chosen option applied.
details: Vanilla does not use it; this follows its name only, so what 'option' means is not certain.

label: Success text
summary: The text describing what happens if the scheme succeeds.
details: Returns text. No line uses it by this exact name on this type; vanilla does use a matching check for whether such a text exists. Going by its name.

label: Scheme target
summary: The character the scheme is aimed at.
details: Vanilla uses it to write the target's name into the scheme name and as a data context in the GUI.

label: Has discovery text
summary: Whether the scheme has a text about what happens when it is discovered.
details: Vanilla uses it and its negation to show or hide the discovery part of the prediction.

label: Has success text
summary: Whether the scheme has a text about what happens when it succeeds.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the success part of the prediction.

label: Replaces a scheme
summary: Whether starting this scheme would replace one that is already running.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the replace warning in the interaction confirmation window.

label: Is secret
summary: Whether the scheme is secret.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide the secrecy part of the interaction GUI.

label: This scheme info
summary: The scheme prediction info itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by the name: vanilla uses other types' .Self to hand the object itself to another function (for example Character.Self). No line uses this one.

label: This title item
summary: The title entry itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more.

label: Size
summary: The width and height of the title entry, as a pair of numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the size of the entry's widget in the title list.

label: Title
summary: The title this entry stands for.
details: The game marks it as a promotion to the title type. Vanilla uses it as a data context and reads the title's name from it.

label: Tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of this title entry.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as the entry's tooltip.

label: Is selectable
summary: Whether the player can pick this title in the interaction.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of the entry.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this title is currently picked.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the entry, and the confirmation window uses it to choose which variable to clear.

label: On click
summary: Runs the title entry's click action.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it when the player clicks the entry.

label: On right click
summary: Runs the title entry's right-click action.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it when the player right-clicks the entry.

label: This title item
summary: The title entry itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by the name: vanilla uses other types' .Self to hand the object itself to another function (for example Character.Self). No line uses this one.

label: This window
summary: The notification window itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more.

label: Primary ally
summary: The main ally shown in the interfere-in-war notification.
details: No line uses it on this type. The call-ally notification window uses a function of the same name as a data context, so this follows its name.

label: Primary enemy
summary: The main enemy shown in the interfere-in-war notification.
details: No line uses it on this type. The call-ally notification window uses a function of the same name as a data context, so this follows its name.

label: Refusal effects text
summary: The text describing what happens if the interference is refused.
details: Returns text. Vanilla does not use it; this follows its name only.

label: Secondary allies
summary: The list of further allies shown in the notification.
details: No line uses it on this type. The call-ally notification window uses a function of the same name as a list source, so this follows its name.

label: Secondary enemies
summary: The list of further enemies shown in the notification.
details: No line uses it on this type. The call-ally notification window uses a function of the same name as a list source, so this follows its name.

label: Has refusal text
summary: Whether the notification has a text about what happens on refusal.
details: Vanilla does not use it; this follows its name only.

label: This window
summary: The notification window itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by the name: vanilla uses other types' .Self to hand the object itself to another function (for example Character.Self). No line uses this one.

label: This window
summary: The interfere-in-war window itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more.

label: Can send offer
summary: Whether the offer can be sent right now.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of the send button in the interfere-in-war window.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the interfere-in-war window.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it on click.

label: Actor
summary: The character who starts the interaction in this window.
details: No line uses it on this type; the lines found use a similar name on other types. This follows its name only.

label: Confirmation window
summary: The character interaction confirmation window connected to this window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context for parts of the interfere-in-war window.

label: Recipient
summary: The character the interaction in this window is aimed at.
details: No line uses it on this type; the lines found use a similar name on other types. This follows its name only.

label: Selected war tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about the war currently selected.
details: Returns text. Vanilla does not use it; this follows its name only.

label: Send offer tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the send-offer part of the window.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the interfere-in-war window.

label: War items
summary: The list of wars the player can pick from in this window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source (datamodel) of the war list.

label: Has wars
summary: Whether there are any wars to pick from.
details: Vanilla uses its negation to show or hide a part of the window when there are no wars.

label: This window
summary: The interfere-in-war window itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by the name: vanilla uses other types' .Self to hand the object itself to another function (for example Character.Self). No line uses this one.

label: Send offer
summary: Sends the offer made in this window.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it on click.

label: This war item
summary: The war list entry itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more.

label: Tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of this war entry.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as the entry's tooltip.

label: War
summary: The war this entry stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the entry, so the entry can show that war.

label: Is enabled
summary: Whether this war can be picked.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of the entry.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this war is the one currently picked.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the entry.

label: On click
summary: Runs the war entry's click action, which picks the war.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it when the entry is clicked; that it picks the war follows from the selected state shown on the same entry.

label: This war item
summary: The war list entry itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by the name: vanilla uses other types' .Self to hand the object itself to another function (for example Character.Self). No line uses this one.

label: This window
summary: The intrigue window itself, as an object that can be passed on.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the intrigue window.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla runs it on click.

label: Expose secret
summary: Exposes a secret of a character using a named interaction.
details: A GUI action with no return value. Vanilla passes a character, the interaction name 'blackmail_interaction' and the secret. What the three values mean exactly is not documented; this follows that one use.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the secret belongs to, going by the vanilla use.
fields.values: a character, as vanilla writes Character.Self

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: A name of the interaction the exposure comes from, going by the vanilla use.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.values: a secret, as vanilla writes Secret.Self

label: Character
summary: The character whose intrigue the window shows.
details: The game marks it as a promotion to the character type. Vanilla uses it as the data context of the window and passes the character on to the countermeasure item.
